title: Context compaction has no preserved-invariant contract, so a summary can silently drop the standing instructions
problem: My agent followed the project rules for two hours, then its history was compacted, and the summary that replaced it did not carry the rules forward - so it kept working confidently without them and nothing told me.
symptom: Behaviour changes at the compaction boundary rather than at a code or prompt change: the agent starts doing things the conventional way, searches the wrong directory, ignores a documented constraint, and one instruction to re-read the rules file restores it immediately.
why_now: Compaction is now the default lever for long-horizon work and ships enabled in coding agents, but every published implementation steers it with a tuned summariser prompt and none of them asserts, after the new context is built, that a named set of standing instructions is still in it. Recall is optimised on average and never verified per run, so a dropped rule and a kept rule produce identical, silent output.
existing: Tuned compaction prompts: raise average recall, but give no per-run guarantee, so the run that drops a rule looks exactly like the run that kept it.
Tool-result clearing: safe precisely because it discards outputs rather than instructions, which is why it does not address instructions being lost.
Re-reading the rules file by hand after each compaction: what users report doing, but it is operator labour triggered by first noticing misbehaviour.
Structured note-taking to an external file: persists what the agent chose to write down, not the constraints the operator imposed on it.

evidence.title: Effective context engineering for AI agents
evidence.quote: overly aggressive compaction can result in the loss of subtle but critical context whose importance only becomes apparent later
evidence.note: The vendor that ships compaction names loss of critical context as the known hazard, and its stated remedy is prompt tuning on traces - an averaging technique, not a per-run assertion that a required instruction survived.

evidence.title: Effective context engineering for AI agents
evidence.quote: Start by maximizing recall to ensure your compaction prompt captures every relevant piece of information from the trace
evidence.note: Confirms the contract is a prompt-quality goal rather than a checked invariant: recall is maximised by iteration, and nothing downstream refuses a compacted context that lost a rule.

evidence.title: [BUG] Claude forgets everything in CLAUDE.md after compaction
evidence.quote: Claude does not remember CLAUDE.md after compaction
evidence.note: A user-filed report of exactly this failure, with the workaround being a manual instruction to re-read the rules file - operator labour standing in for a missing contract.

evidence.title: [BUG] CLAUDE.md instructions completely ignored after context compaction
evidence.quote: If Claude cannot follow CLAUDE.md after compaction, it should warn the user
evidence.note: A second independent report five months later, and the request in it IS the missing primitive: a signal when the compacted context no longer carries the instructions.

build_hypothesis: A compaction post-condition: the operator declares a small set of required instruction strings or ids, and the compactor refuses to hand back a context that does not contain them, re-injecting them verbatim and logging the near-miss instead of continuing silently.

check.manual_question: When your agent compacts or summarises its history, what refuses the new context if a standing instruction is no longer in it, and where is that assertion in the code?
check.rationale: A code path that summarises message history is the compaction step. The gap is the absence of any post-condition on its output, so the check looks for the summariser plus the absence of re-injection or invariant-assertion vocabulary. It can be wrong in two ways worth naming: a repo that merely discusses re-injection in a comment or a doc reads as mitigated (fail-open, which is why mitigated_when is code-only and the manual_question asks where the assertion lives), and a repo that names its compaction step in unusual vocabulary is not matched at all.
